contracts.result: Start and restart resolve true at the requested target and false when superseded; current preparation failure rejects. Stop and destroy return synchronous booleans and callback failures throw.
contracts.timing: Notifications are synchronous and ignore returns. Only prepareStart is awaited with options and an abort context; start completion receives one resolved result. Supersession aborts before replacement preparation. Initial startup is inactive; retained restart stays active with stateEvents delivering. Stop synchronously stops descendants and deactivates before root teardown; destroy synchronously releases child Applications, UI, owned Region, state, Radio and listeners. Suppressed state events are not replayed.
contracts.ownership: Registration never starts children. Callers explicitly await prerequisites. Stop/destroy traverse all owned descendants, including stopped intermediate owners; descendants cannot start/restart during an ancestor stop or terminal phase.
contracts.mutation: Canceled readiness cannot append stale framework completion events or alter stable state.
contracts.repetition: Pending start calls share promises and ignore later options. Stop and destroy are synchronous and idempotent. Each restart reruns preparation without stopping the active run or children; latest intent wins. Start during retained restart resolves true without canceling it. Restart during initial startup supersedes preparation; after stop it starts the stopped feature. Only start selects a Region instance. Active or pending start ignores new options; restart retains its host and ignores forwarded region options. Start/restart cannot activate during cleanup; onStop may start a next run after cleanup. Full reset is explicit stop followed by start. Start joins restart readiness while the Application has no active run. Independently active children remain active when restart prepares a stopped owner.
contracts.destruction: Destruction is terminal during callbacks and blocks owner/descendant activation. It stops descendants before the before:destroy notification, destroys children in registration order, and releases owned resources and incoming/outgoing event subscriptions synchronously. Callback failures throw and abort remaining teardown, without rollback or retry of partial instances.
